title: Radiata Stories
subtitle: A city whose inhabitants have places to be
summary: Radiata Stories is tri-Ace's PlayStation 2 action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 27 January 2005. Jack Russell enters a world of knights, guilds and neighbouring peoples, but much of its character comes from the individuals living around him. Town residents follow daily routines, going to work and returning home instead of waiting permanently in one place. The player learns the city by noticing those movements. body: Radiata Stories is tri-Ace's PlayStation 2 action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 27 January 2005. Jack Russell enters a world of knights, guilds and neighbouring peoples, but much of its character comes from the individuals living around him. Town residents follow daily routines, going to work and returning home instead of waiting permanently in one place. The player learns the city by noticing those movements. Meeting someone can depend on when and where they are approached, making ordinary observation part of building a party and discovering the world.

Characters have their own jobs, homes, personalities and schedules. The day-and-night system gives those details practical consequences, as a person encountered in one place may be elsewhere later. Exploring therefore means paying attention to the habits of the population as well as the geography of the streets. Recruitment grows from those meetings and the tasks attached to them, connecting the party to the larger community. The city gradually becomes more familiar because the player understands who uses it, not only because every doorway has been opened once.

Naoki Akiyama directed the game, with Noriyuki Iwadare composing the soundtrack. Its action combat sits alongside a world whose people provide many reasons to return to familiar places. The North American release followed in September 2005. Reception was mixed at launch, but the game developed a lasting following for its character and approach to everyday life. Radiata Stories makes a useful distinction within the role-playing genre: a large cast can be more than a list of recruits when each member appears to have a life continuing outside the player's immediate journey.
story_headings: A city whose inhabitants have places to be
Learn a routine, then make a connection
An adventure remembered for its population
